title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
summary: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title:
Unfolding
of Field-Free Spin–Orbit Torque Magnetization
Switching in a van der Waals Heterostructure
summary:
Abstract 
                   Heterostructures of 2D materials offer high tunability of magnetic properties, including current-induced magnetization switching by unconventional spin–orbit torques. The microscopic mechanisms governing spin-torque switching in van der Waals systems, however, remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate current-induced magnetization reversal in an Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) and WTe2 heterostructure using scanning harmonic magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy. Spatially resolved magnetization maps show that field-free switching unfolds from asymmetric domain nucleation at the edges of the FGT flake, followed by domain wall propagation. This switching behavior is deterministic and bipolar, consistent with spin–orbit torques arising from the injection of both in-plane and out-of-plane spins from WTe2 into FGT. The critical currents for up-to-down and down-to-up switching differ because of asymmetric domain nucleation and directional domain wall pinning effects. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the switching behavior observed experimentally, showing how the initial domain nucleation sites are determined by the sample geometry and combined influence of in-plane and out-of-plane spins and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Finally, by systematically varying the field-like and damping-like torque components and sweeping the spin polarization between in-plane and out-of-plane, we identify the torque configurations that yield the most efficient switching in van der Waals magnets with different shapes.

title:
Spin-Sensitive
Optical Anisotropy Controlled by Pump
Polarization in the Kagome Antiferromagnet FeSn
summary:
Abstract 
                   Antiferromagnetic (AFM) materials offer ultrafast spin dynamics, negligible stray fields, and robustness against magnetic perturbations, yet their vanishing net magnetization renders optical detection and control of the Néel vector fundamentally challenging. Here, we demonstrate pump-polarization-written optical and magneto-optical (MO) anisotropy in the Kagome AFM FeSn by using pump–probe ultrafast spectroscopy. The experimental findings reveal that the principal axes of both optical and MO anisotropies are dictated exclusively by the pump polarization but remain insensitive to sample rotation, ruling out lattice birefringence as the dominant origin. Linearly polarized excitation generates a photoinduced electronic polarization that couples efficiently to AFM order via spin-layer-locked Dirac Fermions. In parallel, a cooperative anisotropic deformation potential mechanism produces bond-selective transient strain that modifies the dielectric tensor through elasto-optic and spin–orbit coupling, becoming increasingly prominent at higher fluence. These results establish a deterministic and nonthermal control of spin-sensitive optical anisotropy by pump polarization in Kagome AFMs.

title: Engineering‐Free Deterministic Spin‐Orbit Torque Switching in Ultrathin Perpendicular Synthetic Antiferromagnets
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   Spin‐orbit torque (SOT) offers a promising route for energy‐efficient magnetization manipulation in low‐power spintronic devices. Synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) structure, in particular, enhances device performance through ultrafast magnetization switching and magnetic stray‐field resilience. However, achieving deterministic SOT switching in perpendicularly magnetized SAFs typically requires an additional in‐plane magnetic field or structural engineering to break inversion symmetry, which complicates their practical implementation. Here, we demonstrate field‐free deterministic SOT switching in ultra‐thin perpendicular SAFs operating at room temperature, designed with a symmetric CoFeB (0.6 nm)/W/CoFeB (0.6 nm) structure. This switching occurs only under antiferromagnetic coupling conditions between the two CoFeB layers, and the switching chirality can be tuned via the spacer layer thickness and temperature. Micromagnetic modeling reveals that symmetry breaking arises intrinsically from the interplay between Ruderman‐Kittel‐Kasuya‐Yosida and Dzyaloshinskii‐Moriya interactions, which stabilize the asymmetric Néel‐Bloch mixed domain walls of both CoFeB layers. These domain walls manifest as dynamic spin textures with a net chiral driving force, enabling deterministic magnetization switching without the need for external fields or engineered structural asymmetry. Our findings provide a streamlined path toward practical applications of ultrathin SAFs in structurally simplified, fabrication‐friendly SOT memory and logic devices.

title: Field‐Free Switching of Spin–Orbit Torque Magnetic Devices via Symmetry Breaking: An Overview and Outlook
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   Spin–orbit torque (SOT) technology stands at the forefront of next‐generation non‐volatile memory and logic computing, promising superior endurance and ultrafast dynamics compared to conventional spin‐transfer torque (STT) architectures. However, the persistent requirement of an external magnetic field for deterministic switching of perpendicular magnetization severely impedes high‐density integration and commercial viability. This review systematically evaluates the evolutionary trajectory of symmetry‐breaking strategies developed to overcome this bottleneck. The analysis progresses from early macroscopic structural engineering, such as wedged geometries and lateral asymmetries, to mesoscopic built‐in effective fields driven by interfacial exchange coupling and chiral spin textures. Crucially, we identify a defining paradigm shift in the field: the transition from complex geometric modifications toward intrinsic material‐level innovations, including low‐symmetry crystals, vertical composition gradients (VCG), and synergistic dual‐torque (STT‐SOT) architectures. By resolving the trade‐offs among switching efficiency, thermal stability, and structural complexity, these intrinsic and hybrid approaches offer a practical roadmap for integrating scalable, all‐electrical SOT‐MRAM with standard CMOS back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL) processes. Finally, we establish a dual‐track strategic roadmap: while long‐term breakthroughs require parallel exploration of new exotic physics, we underscore the importance of focusing on mass production and foundry scalability at the current stage.

title: Analog Spin–Orbit Torque Switching in Vertically Graded Pt/Co–Re Heterostructures for Neuromorphic Computing
summary:
Abstract 
                   Achieving gradual, analog magnetization switching in spin–orbit torque (SOT) devices is essential for neuromorphic computing. In perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA)-based SOT devices, gradual switching can arise from domain nucleation, domain-wall propagation, and pinning, and controlling it through materials design remains a key goal. This study demonstrates that a vertically graded cobalt (Co)–rhenium (Re) alloy region, formed through a simple Co/Re multilayer design, enables analog SOT switching in Pt/Co–Re heterostructures. Microstructural and compositional analyses confirm that annealing transforms the discrete multilayer into a depth-dependent alloy with tunable gradient direction and magnitude, controlled by adjusting the Re layer thickness distribution. Increasing the Co/Re bilayer repetition number up to 3 yields a pronounced sigmoid-like transfer characteristic plausibly explained by the sequential reversal of sub-regions with distributed local switching thresholds, with only a small change in the effective PMA energy. We demonstrate stable, bidirectional long-term potentiation and depression under repeated pulse stimulation across Re compositions of 30–70%. System-level validation using a multilayer perceptron on MNIST (modified National Institute of Standards and Technology) Digits, Fashion-MNIST, and MNIST Characters datasets shows test accuracies within 1.21 percentage points of the ideal sigmoid baseline, with MNIST Digits accuracy varying by 0.24 percentage points across the full compositional range.

summary:
Abstract

Hardware Acceleration of Stochastic Neural Networks Enabled by Bit‐Cell Level Co‐Design of Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   Processing‐in‐memory architectures mitigate data shuttling bottlenecks in deterministic AI workloads, but still depend on costly external entropy sources for probabilistic models. Here, we present a magnetic‐tunnel‐junction‐based processing‐in‐memory architecture that unifies data storage and massively parallel probabilistic computation for stochastic and deterministic neural networks. By introducing bit‐paired stochastic and stable magnetic tunnel junctions, we realize a multi‐precision stochastic memory cell that transduces stored binary weights into variance‐tunable stochastic bitstreams in situ. We evaluate the architecture's versatility across three progressive regimes of stochastic neural computation. First, by using a hardware‐in‐the‐loop prototype interfacing fabricated stochastic spin‐orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions with a field‐programmable gate array chip, we validate stochastic matrix‐vector multiplications and achieve near‐floating‐point accuracy without specialized retraining. Second, for networks with stochastic neurons, we demonstrate an Ising machine that utilizes adaptive‐precision sampling and dynamic graph routing to reduce time‐to‐solution. Third, we propose an in‐memory Bayesian computer with independent control of weight means and uncertainties, and apply it to a localization problem under unreliable inputs. By keeping intermediate signals in the stochastic domain, the architecture reduces peripheral overhead associated with random‐number generation and data conversion. This device‐circuit co‐design provides a shared hardware platform for stochastic neural inference, combinatorial optimization, and uncertainty‐aware computing.

Toward an Ideal S = 1/2 Kagome Antiferromagnet and Quantum Spin Liquid Candidate through Selective Mg 2+ Doping of Averievite
summary:
Abstract 
                   Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are exotic states of matter where geometric frustration and quantum fluctuations suppress conventional magnetic order. S = 1/2 kagome antiferromagnets (KAFMs) are an ideal platform for realizing such behavior, and several mineral-inspired Cu2+-based kagome systems have emerged as promising candidates. Among these, Averievite (Cu5V2O10CsCl) offers a structurally distinct route to frustrated magnetism through its copper oxovanadate framework, which hosts alternating kagome and honeycomb layers. Prior studies have shown that targeted Zn2+ substitution on the honeycomb CuH site can suppress magnetic order and promote QSL-like behavior. Here we investigate Mg2+ substitution in the Averievite family, motivated by the geometric flexibility and favorable scattering contrast of Mg2+ relative to Zn2+, the previously explored diamagnetic dopant. Herein we present the novel MgxCu5–xV2O10CsCl (x = 0, 0.5, 1, 2) family, utilizing X-ray diffraction, single-crystal electron diffraction, and SQUID magnetometry to obtain precise structural parameters, including site occupancies, antisite disorder, and local coordination information, and to correlate these with the varied magnetic behavior. Increasing Mg2+ content leads to a pronounced suppression of both the structural and long-range magnetic ordering, alongside an increased mean field antiferromagnetic interaction, signaling enhanced magnetic frustration. Crucially, electron diffraction data is indicative of less than 1% Mg2+ antisite disorder onto the kagome lattice in the Mg2 compound. This contrasts with Zn-based analogues, preserving the integrity of the S = 1/2 kagome network. At x = 2, neither long-range order nor spin freezing is observed down to 2K, giving a new S = 1/2 KAFM with early hallmarks of QSL behavior and establishing Mg-doped Averievite as a clean and highly tunable platform for exploring QSL ground states.

summary:
Abstract 
                   
                    Spin-orbit torque (SOT) enables efficient manipulation of magnetization. Owing to its advantages of high speed, superior endurance, and low power consumption, SOT is attractive for non-volatile memory and logic devices, and emerges as a core writing mechanism for next-generation magnetic random-access memory. In conventional heavy-metal/ferromagnet heterostructures, the spin Hall effect generates only in-plane spin polarization. Consequently, deterministic SOT switching of perpendicular magnetization relies on an external magnetic field to break symmetry, which imposes a critical limitation on high-density device integration. Over the past several decades, field-free switching has been realized through various strategies, such as wedge-shaped films, composition grading, exchange bias, and canted magnetic moments. However, these approaches typically suffer from slow switching speed, high power consumption, and complex fabrication. Low-symmetry van der Waals (vdW) topological semimetals—including WTe
                     2 
                    , TaIrTe
                     4 
                    , and NbIrTe
                     4 
                    —offer a fundamentally new route for field-free switching. Originating from intrinsic crystal symmetry breaking, their unconventional spin polarization drives robust field-free SOT switching without relying on an external magnetic field. This review systematically summarizes the evolution of field-free SOT switching. We analyze the intrinsic bottlenecks of conventional SOT architectures, then elaborate various categories of symmetry-breaking strategies toward field-free switching, and highlight the unique merits of low-symmetry vdW spin-source materials. In addition, we discuss functional implementations of all-vdW SOT spintronic devices for in-memory logic, nonvolatile magnetic memory, and neuromorphic computing, and conclude by outlining unresolved challenges and prospective research pathways.

ABSTRACT 
                   Kagome‐lattice magnets provide a fertile ground for exploring exotic electronic phases due to topological band structures and complex magnetic orders. Yet, how these ingredients dictate unconventional magnetotransport responses, crucial for possible spintronic applications, has remained elusive. Here, we show that a prototypical kagome antiferromagnet  exhibits significant magnetic‐field‐driven redistribution of Berry curvature and the colossal anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC). Under high magnetic fields, spin canting induces a pronounced spin splitting of the flat and Dirac bands near the Fermi level, dramatically enhancing the Berry curvature. This colossal AHC enhancement is attributed to a synergy between field‐tuned Berry curvature and enhanced skew scattering in the clean limit. Our findings highlight the critical role of magnetic‐field‐controlled spin splitting in engineering Berry curvature and anomalous magnetotransport in clean kagome magnets.

title: Six-state manipulation of Mn3Sn via spin–orbit torque
summary: The electrical control of the magnetic octupole in chiral antiferromagnets is essential for advanced spintronic devices. Based on atomistic spin model simulations, this work investigates the dynamical behavior of spin–orbit torque (SOT)-driven magnetic state switching in the chiral antiferromagnet Mn3Sn. By precisely tuning the amplitude and width of the current pulses, deterministic and sequential switching of the magnetic octupole moment among its six energy-degenerate states can be achieved. The unidirectional out-of-plane lifting of the magnetic moments from the kagome plane during the pulse duration governs the post-pulse precession of the magnetic octupole and determines its final state after relaxation. Furthermore, this work verifies that the stable states of Mn3Sn exhibit a clock-like stepping switching behavior under the action of sequential current pulses. This study reveals the ultrafast manipulation mechanism of the six-state magnetic order of Mn3Sn driven by SOT, providing a theoretical foundation for developing multi-state spintronic devices.

title:
Tunable Magnetotransport across Competing Magnetic
Phases in the Distorted Kagome Antiferromagnet HoPtSn
summary:
Abstract 
                   Competing magnetic phases in frustrated systems provide a fertile ground for unusual magnetic and electronic responses owing to their sensitivity to external perturbations. The distorted kagome antiferromagnet HoPtSn is an example of such a system, exhibiting successive magnetic transitions and multiple field-induced metamagnetic states at low temperatures. Here, we combine magnetic susceptibility, heat capacity, magnetotransport, and magnetization under hydrostatic pressure measurements on single crystals to investigate the interplay between the competing magnetic phases in HoPtSn. At ambient pressure, HoPtSn undergoes two magnetic transitions at TN1 ≈ 7.3 K and TN2 ≈ 2.7 K. The lower-temperature transition is accompanied by pronounced thermal and magnetic hysteresis, indicating its first-order character. Magnetization measurements reveal a series of field-induced transitions and a strongly anisotropic low-temperature phase diagram. Correspondingly, the magnetotransport exhibits sharp anomalies across the metamagnetic transitions together with clear field-history dependence, while Hall resistivity measurements reveal additional features that emerge within the ordered state. These results point to a strong coupling between electronic transport and magnetic reconstruction. Hydrostatic pressure leaves TN1 nearly unchanged, while it gradually shifts TN2 to higher temperatures, indicating that the competing magnetic phases respond differently to lattice compression, while the first-order transition remains robust throughout the investigated pressure range. Electronic structure calculations reveal several Dirac-like crossings near the Fermi level, suggesting possible interplay between these features and the complex magnetic phase space. Taken together, our results show that HoPtSn hosts a delicate balance between competing magnetic states, whose reconstruction leaves distinct signatures in the transport properties and can be continuously tuned by pressure. These findings highlight distorted kagome antiferromagnets as a promising platform for exploring the interplay between magnetic phase competition and electronic transport.

Energy landscape of the kagome antiferromagnet: characterization of multiple energy scales
summary:
Abstract 
                   We investigate the energy landscape of the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet within its coplanar ground-state manifold. Although coplanar states are degenerate at harmonic order, transitions between them require collective weathervane-loop rotations whose barriers grow strongly with loop size. To characterize this structure, we construct disconnectivity graphs using two complementary approaches: exact enumeration and minimax-barrier calculations for small lattices, and a statistical construction for large lattices based on random walks through configuration space, with loop length used as a proxy for barrier height. The exact landscape reveals a dominant low-barrier scale associated with elementary six-spin loops and a broader higher-barrier sector from longer rearrangements. For large systems, the statistical analysis exposes a hierarchy of barrier scales, including a pronounced six-spin-loop peak and an intermediate scale-free regime of loop lengths. This hierarchy provides a natural basis for multiple dynamical time scales: six-spin loops govern the fastest local relaxation, while slower collective dynamics arise from activation of longer loops. These results show that the coplanar manifold is dynamically rugged, with its low-energy dynamics governed by a hierarchy of loop-mediated barriers.

title: Spatially asymmetric switching under spin–orbit torque and Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction
summary: Efficient spin–orbit torque (SOT) switching of perpendicular magnetization is of crucial importance for the magnetic random-access memory. We find that the magnetization reversal occurs first at the corner of the sample and then propagates to the whole sample through domain-wall motion. We show that, in the absence of field-like SOT, the location of this anti-domain nucleation corner exhibits left-right and top-down asymmetries, as determined by the polarities of current and Hx. By varying the magnitude and sign of field-like SOT, we establish that it significantly affects the switching process but is not necessary for such switching asymmetries. These results are fully explained using a consistent torque analysis framework. Our work improves the understanding of the physics behind SOT switching.

title: Achieving low write error rates in perpendicular spin–orbit torque MRAM: A micromagnetic modeling feasibility study

title: Computing with Coupled Oscillator Networks: Optimization, Memory, and Modern AI Primitives
summary: We explore how synchronization in coupled oscillator networks may be employed to perform a variety of computing tasks. These systems are becoming more attractive as an alternative to conventional digital computers due to the increasing energy demands of the latter, particularly for large-scale problems in machine learning and artificial intelligence. The ubiquity of coupled oscillator networks means that oscillator-based computing can be thought of as a universal computing paradigm encompassing systems with a diversity of physical realizations, e.g. as analog circuits, neurological systems, spintronic systems. The bridge between the dynamics of coupled oscillator networks and computational primitives they implement is the Ising model, which originates in statistical physics, and when applied to oscillator networks, explains the emergence of globally complex and disordered synchronization patterns from local interactions in the network. Second, oscillator networks as associative memory systems, enabling storage and retrieval of data represented through phases of oscillations. Finally, oscillator networks as a dynamical implementation of attention, with synchronization providing the mechanism for the alignment of keys to queries. The ability of oscillator networks to implement these computational primitives paves the way for novel realizations of intelligent systems through a variety of physical substrates.

title: Non-Volatile Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
summary: This chapter explores the critical role of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) devices in advancing neuromorphic computing. Inspired by the human brain's remarkable ability to perform complex tasks like pattern recognition and adaptation, neuromorphic computing offers immense potential for implementing complex neural networks (NNs) in real hardware. Despite ongoing research into the brain's complexities, its fundamental operation relies on neurons (processing units communicating via electrochemical signals) and synapses (junctions between neurons). The modifiable strength of the synapse is key to learning and memory functionality, allowing the brain to adapt and rewire itself. For dense and low-power circuits in neuromorphic computing, these eNVM devices are ideal due to their synaptic-like behavior and non-volatile information storage. Properties such as conductance modulation of these devices emulate synaptic plasticity, which is crucial for learning, and their scalability makes them promising for large-scale neuromorphic architectures. This chapter will delve into the various types of eNVM devices such as resistive RAM (ReRAM), phase-change memory (PCM), spintronics-based memory devices, and their applications in neuromorphic computing, discussing their challenges and opportunities, and highlighting recent advances in their integration within neuromorphic systems.

title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet

title: Cooperative STT and SOT switching in perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions: Role of the pulse-end magnetization state
summary: Spin--orbit torque MRAM (SOT-MRAM) is a leading candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory, offering high speed, endurance, and architectural compatibility. ABSTRACT

The model further serves as a high-throughput pre-screening tool for external discovery spaces, rapidly prioritizing candidate TSMs before expensive first-principles or experimental validation. Representative TXL-prioritized candidates were subsequently supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, demonstrating the practical value of the framework for reducing discovery cost. By uniting symbolic chemical rules, statistical learning, and language-based representations, TXL Fusion provides a scalable and interpretable strategy for accelerating the discovery of next-generation topological and quantum materials.

title: Magnetic-field controlled organic spintronic memristor for neural network computation

Driven by fluorine atom migration within the PVDF layer, the device demonstrates both long-term depression (LTD) and long-term potentiation (LTP) under controlled electrical polarization. Distinctively, the resistance states can also be modulated by an external magnetic field via the tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) effect, introducing a non-electrical means of tuning synaptic plasticity. This magnetic control mechanism enables multi-state modulation without compromising device performance or endurance. Furthermore, convolutional neural network (CNN) simulations incorporating this magnetic tuning capability reveal enhanced pattern recognition accuracy and improved training stability, especially at high learning rates. title: Field Free Spin-Orbit Torque Controlled Synapse and Stochastic Neuron Devices for Spintronic Boltzmann Neural Networks

title: Magnetic field effects on spin-split band and magnon transport in altermagnets and emergent compensated ferrimagnets
summary: In altermagnets and fully compensated ferrimagnets, not only the electron band but also the magnon band exhibits spin splitting without net magnetization, which enables thermal activation of the magnon spin current. Here, we theoretically investigate magnetic field effects on the magnon properties of these antiferromagnets in the presence of a weak easy-axis anisotropy which makes the collinear states robust against the magnetic field. For the altermagnet and compensated ferrimagnet, we analyze a 2 sublattice order in the $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_2^\prime$ model on the square lattice and a triple-${\bf Q}$ 12-sublattice order in the $J_1$-$J_3$ model on the kagome lattice, respectively, each accompanied by $d$-wave and $s$-wave spin splitting at zero field. It is shown that for positive (negative) magnetic field $H$ whose energy scale is smaller than the anisotropy gap, the up- and down-spin magnon bands are shifted to lower (higher) and higher (lower) energies, respectively, similarly to the Zeeman coupling in electron systems. In the altermagnet, with increasing field, the $d$-wave splitting tends to be deformed into the $s$-wave one, which is reflected as the change in the direction of the spin current generated by thermal gradient. In the compensated ferrimagnet, the $s$-wave nature, i.e., the population imbalance between the up- and down-spin magnons at $H=0$, can induce an asymmetric field dependence of the longitudinal spin and thermal conductivities in a field-sweep process.

title: Machine-learning-accelerated discovery of synthesizable high-temperature altermagnets with giant spin splitting
summary: Altermagnets offer a route to spin-polarized electronic states without macroscopic magnetization, because compensated magnetic order can generate momentum-dependent spin splitting through crystal-symmetry-controlled exchange fields. However, experimentally viable altermagnets combining large spin splitting, thermodynamic stability and high magnetic ordering temperatures remain scarce. Here, we develop a machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput framework to explore the tetragonal AB$_2$C$_2$D compounds. Screening 8640 variants identifies 1347 compensated antiferromagnetic candidates satisfying altermagnetic symmetry. An interpretable XGBoost model trained on first-principles spin-splitting data then isolates 34 low-hull-energy candidates,including four previously reported, with giant non-relativistic spin splittings exceeding 1.5 eV near the Fermi level. Detailed first-principles calculations of the representative RbMn$_2$Te$_2$O confirm a maximum spin splitting of $\sim$1.88 eV with dynamical stability and an estimated Néel temperature of $\sim$390 K. The giant splitting originates from symmetry-locked Mn-sublattice exchange fields amplified by directional Mn-d/Te-p hybridization. Furthermore, we uncover a profound soft-mode-driven structural transition associated with an interlayer dimensionality crossover in SrMn$_2$Te$_2$O, yet the unfolded electronic structure demonstrates that the altermagnetic spin splitting remains robust after lattice reconstruction. Hydrostatic pressure provides an additional tuning route, producing non-monotonic modulation of the spin-split Fermi surface governed by local coordination and orbital hybridization. These results establish tetragonal AB$_2$C$_2$D compounds as a tunable materials platform for stray-field-free spintronic devices and provide a general data-driven strategy for discovering robust giant-splitting altermagnets.

title: Epitaxial Magnon Junctions with Y3Fe5O12/Gd3Ga5O12/Pt-nanoparticles/Y3Fe5O12
summary: The excitation, propagation, manipulation, and detection of magnons lie at the core of magnonics. Among various device architectures, high-quality magnon junctions with a ferromagnetic insulator (FI)/antiferromagnetic insulator (AFI)/ferromagnetic insulator (FI) configuration are predicted to exhibit a near-100% magnon junction ratio (MJR), making them promising candidates for high-performance non-volatile memory applications. Yttrium iron garnet (Y3Fe5O12, YIG) is widely employed as the FI material in such structures for its exceptionally low magnetic damping. However, in previously reported magnon junctions, the epitaxial relationship between the two YIG layers is often disrupted by lattice-mismatched AFI spacers. Although this leads to distinct coercivities, it simultaneously degrades the crystalline quality of the top YIG layer, thereby limiting the magnontransmission efficiency. Here, an epitaxial magnon junction is demonstrated incorporating a hybrid Gd3Ga5O12 (GGG)/Pt-nanoparticles spacer that maintains coherent epitaxy while enabling an antiparallel magnetic configuration. Compared with nickel oxide-based magnon junctions, the coercivity-tuned top YIG layer in our structure exhibits superior crystalline quality and much lower magnetic damping. A clear magnon junction effect is observed with a 43% MJR achieved. The interlayer coupling between the two ferrimagnetic insulators is found to enhance the MJR. These results offer valuable insights for the development of advanced magnon-based spintronic devices.

title: Sign reversal of ST-FMR signals in CoFeB/Pt explained by contributions beyond spin-orbit torque
summary: Spin-orbit torques (SOT) provide an efficient route for electrical control of magnetization and is of central interest for low-power magnetic memory applications. Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) is a widely used technique to quantify SOT efficiencies. However, the rectified voltage measured in ST-FMR can contain contributions that are not directly related to SOTs, which affects the accuracy of the extracted torque efficiencies. This may contribute to the large variation of reported SOT efficiencies in literature. In this study, we investigate the damping-like torque efficiencies in CoFeB/Pt heterostructures as a function of Pt thickness. Conventional ST-FMR analysis yields an apparent sign reversal of the extracted efficiency at a Pt thickness of approximately 10 nm. By combining complementary measurement geometries and analysis approaches, we separate the torque-induced signal from additional voltage contributions that share the same angular dependence. Our results show that non-torque voltage contributions can produce an apparent sign reversal in conventional ST-FMR analysis, highlighting the need to distinguish SOT-induced signals from parasitic contributions and we show how to reliably determine the SOT efficiencies.

title: Pulse Laser Deposited GaFeO3 Thin Film Grown on FTO: Correlated Ferroic Orders and Strong Magnetodielectric Coupling at Room Temperature
summary: Room-temperature single-phase multiferroics exhibiting coupled ferroelectric and magnetic order are promising candidates for next-generation magnetoelectric memory and spintronic technologies. Here, we report the growth of approximately 100.6 nm thick polycrystalline orthorhombic GaFeO3 thin films on fluorine-doped tin oxide-coated glass (FTO) substrates by pulsed laser deposition. Core-level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a reduced Fe2+ concentration and suppressed oxygen-vacancy formation, contributing to reduced leakage current and improved ferroelectric characteristics. The films exhibit robust ferrimagnetism and ferroelectricity at room temperature, confirming the coexistence of ferroic orders within a single phase. Piezoresponse Force Microscopy further demonstrates reversible local polarization switching, accompanied by an asymmetric butterfly loop with coercive voltages of -0.31 V and +1.07 V. The films also exhibit a high relative dielectric constant of approximately 1700 with a relatively low dielectric loss tangent of approximately 2.83 at 1 MHz. Moreover, a significant magnetodielectric coefficient of approximately 2.3% is observed under a relatively small magnetic field of only 0.1 kOe, highlighting strong magnetoelectric coupling. These results establish GaFeO3 thin films as a promising platform for room-temperature multifunctional devices, mainly low-field magnetoelectric memory and spintronic architectures.

title: Spin-Polarized Weyl Fermions and Unconventional Spin Transport
summary: Large and electrically controllable spin splitting in nonmagnetic materials is highly desirable for condensed-matter physics and spintronics, enabling strongly spin-polarized quasiparticles and unconventional spin transport as well as their electrical control. Here, we establish a general framework for critical spin-polarized Weyl fermions in two-dimensional (2D) nonmagnetic systems. We predict the $α$-Bi-like Group-V puckered-layer family of 2D ferroelectrics as a material platform combining critical spin-Weyl fermions, giant spin splitting, and electrically switchable nonlinear and spin transport. Our calculations reveal exchange-scale spin splitting induced by spin-orbit coupling and a $p$-wave spin texture in the BiAs monolayer. Moreover, BiAs hosts four critical spin-Weyl points, each formed within a single-spin channel. The nearly quantized $\langle S_z\rangle$ is protected by an emergent $S_z$-conservation symmetry in the low-energy limit. The spin-Weyl cones also give rise to unconventional spin-transport phenomena, including a purely out-of-plane Edelstein response and a pronounced spin Nernst effect. Ferroelectric reversal further enables electrical switching of the $p$-wave spin texture and inversion-odd responses, while the tunability of these properties through composition, strain, and magnetic field is also systematically demonstrated across the entire family. These results establish both a general nonmagnetic framework and a promising material platform for exploring critical spin-Weyl physics, nonlinear Hall phenomena, and unconventional spin transport.

title: Finite-Temperature Magnetism and Longitudinal Spin Transport in Compensated Half-Metal Ferrimagnets with Near-Zero Magnetization
summary: Fully compensated ferrimagnets, characterized by nearly vanishing magnetic moments at zero temperature, perfect spin-polarized electronic structures, and ultrafast spin dynamics, represent a highly promising materials platform for next-generation spintronic devices. By minimizing stray magnetic fields and reducing switching currents, FCFs enable a viable path toward high-speed, low-power spintronic devices. In this work, we present a systematic investigation of the electronic structure, finite-temperature magnetism, and spin-dependent transport properties of the Heusler-type fully compensated half-metallic ferrimagnet Mn3Al in magnetic tunnel junctions. We demonstrate that Mn3Al is a half-metallic FCF with 100% spin polarization and fully compensated magnetization at 0 K. Combining density functional theory with Monte Carlo simulations, we characterize its finite-temperature magnetic properties and show that Mn3Al exhibits a net magnetization below 11.6 emu/cc at 300 K, confirming the robustness of its nearly compensated ferrimagnetic order at room temperature. Furthermore, we predict that the Mn3Al/MgO/Mn3Al MTJ yields a giant tunneling magnetoresistance effect at 0 K, which remains as high as 232% at 300 K. Our results establish Mn3Al and related half-metallic FCFs as excellent candidates for magnetoresistance-based spintronic applications.

title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems
summary: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical method for reconstructing energy-level degeneracies and thermodynamic properties of spin systems. A single ancilla qubit is used to measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures. For spectra lying on a known equally spaced energy grid, the inverse discrete Fourier transform allows exact reconstruction of degeneracies in the absence of noise, without spectral leakage. The quantum circuits are optimized using commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering. We demonstrate the method for frustrated Ising antiferromagnets on periodic Kagome graphs with up to 36 spins, using the ibm_kingston quantum processor. Despite substantial circuit depth and hardware noise, the reconstructed spectra retain their dominant features, and the calculated heat capacities reproduce the main temperature dependence of the exact results. Keywords: partition function, imaginary temperature, Ising model, heat capacity, ancilla qubit, quantum computing.

title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
summary: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A $180^\circ$ reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a $π$ phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extracted current density of $7.4\times10^{9}$ A/m$^2$ is, to our knowledge, the lowest reported value for the room-temperature Néel vector switching and we show that it scales with the in-plane uniaxial anisotropy both experimentally and numerically. Synthetic staggered fields and the resonance-based methodology provide a research platform for nanoscale characterisation of electrically driven antiferromagnetic textures, guiding the development of high-frequency on-chip spintronic architectures.

title: Controllable charge-spin conversion in sliding multiferroic metal Fe3GaTe2
summary: Controlling charge--spin conversion within a single magnetic material is important for compact spintronic devices. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, and Wannier-based linear response, we study the Edelstein and spin Hall responses of sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2}. Two degenerate ground states with opposite interlayer sliding vectors and out-of-plane dipole moments are separated by a calculated switching barrier of about $16.3$~meV per unit cell. Magnetization orientation determines the allowed current-induced spin components, while ferroelectric switching induces component-selective sign reversals governed by $M_z\mathcal T$ for in-plane magnetization and by $M_z$ for out-of-plane magnetization. The Edelstein response is strongly energy dependent, with spin accumulation approaching $2~\hbar$ for $\mathbf m\parallel+y$ under a reference field of $1$~V/Å. Momentum-resolved analysis links the TR-even and TR-odd Edelstein responses to $Γ$-centered constant-energy contours and localized interband features, respectively. Spin-conductivity contributions show the opposite momentum-space character, with broad sign-competing spin Berry curvature for TR-even and narrow Fermi-surface contours for TR-odd. The transverse spin Hall conductivity reaches $\sim10^{3}\,(\hbar/e)(\mathrm{S/cm})$ and depends strongly on ferroelectric state and magnetization direction. Magnetization rotations in the $xy$ and $xz$ planes reveal symmetry-allowed higher angular harmonics in both spin accumulation and spin-current responses. These results establish sliding-ferroelectric bilayer \ce{Fe3GaTe2} as a tunable platform for reconfigurable spin accumulation and spin-current generation.

title: Light-induced local control of magnetic anisotropy and domain pattern in Co/Pt multilayers
summary: Control of magnetic anisotropy is essential for the fabrication of next-generation devices in spintronics and magnetic memory. By employing a multi-scale approach combining Kerr microscopy, magnetic force microscopy, and vibrating sample magnetometry, we reveal that low-fluence irradiation enables a reversible, helicity-dependent accumulation of magnetic phases without altering the intrinsic quasistatic properties. Conversely, high-fluence exposure acts as localized thermal annealing that permanently hardens the magnetic system. This structural relaxation leads to a substantial enhancement of the effective perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, driving a twofold increase in the local coercive field and expanding the equilibrium stripe domain width. By offering both reversible spin manipulation and deterministic engineering of 2D magnetic landscapes, this work paves the way towards flexible, lithography-free anisotropy structuring for advanced spintronic applications.

title: Interlocked Vortex Order in the Frustrated $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ Lattice ($A$=Cs,Rb)
summary: Recently synthesized $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ ($A$ = Cs, Rb) provides a unique platform for exploring the interplay between geometric frustration, magnetism, and correlated electronic states beyond conventional kagome systems. In addition, the Heisenberg model analysis show strong constraints on the ground state magnetic configuration, such that fixing spin configuration of 1 triangle propagates and fixes all others. The vortex or anti-vortex phase hosts electronic structures reminiscent of kagome metals, including Dirac-like band crossings, van Hove singularities, and flat bands near the Fermi level. Owing to the noncollinear spin texture and quasi-two-dimensional magnetic character, the Néel temperature exhibits an extremely weak dependence on both the magnitude and direction of external magnetic fields, consistent with experimental observations. For Cs-based compound, the ground state band structure is metallic with 6 Weyl points in the BZ; while for the Rb-based compound, spin--orbit coupling opens an approximately 27-meV gap at ambient pressure due to the lifted C$_3$ symmetry. Our results establish $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ as a promising platform for studying frustration-driven chiral magnetism and its interplay with topological electronic states.

title: Flat-band ferrimagnetism in the edge-centered honeycomb antiferromagnet: From harmonic flat magnon to broad continuum
summary: One of the most striking aspects of a flat band is not merely its lack of dispersion, but that it reduces the single-particle kinetic energy to a very small scale, allowing interaction effects to become the dominant energy scale in the low-energy physics. This picture has underpinned concepts such as flat-band ferromagnetism, flat-band superconductivity, and localized magnons. A more fundamental question, however, remains. Flat bands belong to the language of single-particle or linear-spin-wave physics; whether they survive as protected sharp excitations in a genuine many-body quantum magnet, or merely provide a skeleton of spectral weight left by the noninteracting picture, remains unclear. We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the edge-centered honeycomb lattice to examine this question. In contrast to flat bands in geometrically frustrated magnets such as kagome, this lattice has a 2:3 sublattice imbalance that renders the intersublattice coupling matrix rectangular, whose null space gives rise to a flat band at the single-particle level. The same imbalance stabilizes a ferrimagnetic ground state through the Lieb--Mattis theorem and leads to an edge-site-localized flat magnon in linear spin-wave theory. Combining linear spin-wave theory, sign-problem-free stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo, and stochastic analytic continuation, we find that quantum fluctuations transform this harmonic flat mode into a broad continuum whose centroid is about 1.55J and nearly dispersionless along the high-symmetry path. Sublattice imbalance thus offers an unfrustrated route that unifies flat bands and ferrimagnetism, and suggests that flat-band geometry organizes many-body spectral weight rather than giving rise to a protected quasiparticle.

title: Confinement-deconfinement transitions in the dimer-loop models on two-dimensional non-bipartite lattices
summary: Recent work [Kundu, Damle, Phys. Rev. X 15, 011018 (2025)] has demonstrated that a class of $S=1$ kagome lattice antiferromagnets with competing anisotropies can exhibit unusual low-temperature behavior that is best described in terms of the statistical mechanics of an interesting interpolation between the fully-packed dimer model and the fully-packed loop model on the bipartite honeycomb lattice. On this and other bipartite lattices in two and three dimension, such fully-packed dimer-loop models generically have two distinct power-law correlated Coulomb phases, both of which admit a low-energy description in terms of a fluctuating divergence-free polarization vector field [Phys. Rev. X 15, 011018 (2025); arXiv:2510.11607]. The transition between these phases corresponds to a confinement transition for the $Z_2$ part of the corresponding $U(1)$ flux [Phys. Rev. X 15, 011018 (2025); arXiv:2510.11607]. Here we demonstrate that a variant of such a topological confinement transition can also exist in dimer-loop models on non-bipartite lattices such as the kagome and triangular lattices although the low-energy description does not feature any conserved $U(1)$ flux. In these non-bipartite dimer-loop models, both phases are short-range correlated liquids, and the topological distinction between them is in terms of a $Z_2$-valued winding number instead of the flux of a divergence-free polarization field. In spite of this key difference, this transition appears to be in the same Ising universality class as the analogous transition of the bipartite dimer-loop models. These kagome and triangular lattice dimer-loop models correspond respectively to the low-energy limit of a class of $S=1$ antiferromagnets with competing anisotropies on the ruby lattice comprising a corner-sharing arrangement of fully-frustrated squares and a lattice of corner-sharing fully-frustrated hexagons.

title: The effects of non-stoichiometric lattice structure and secondary phase α-Fe2O3 on modifying the magnetic, electrical, and magneto-electric properties of Eu doped BaFe12O19 hexaferrite
summary: The Ba-atoms in BaFe12O19 were substituted by Eu-atoms to prepare the material of composition Ba1-xEuyFe12O19. The Eu atoms occupied at the sites of Fe atoms. The atomic ratio of Eu/Ba were varied from 0 to 0.33 to control the secondary phase (hematite) and M-type hexaferrite. Raman spectra provided complimentary support for a systematic increase of the hematite phase on increasing the Eu/Ba ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy informed the presence of oxygen deficiency and surface defects, and charge state of Ba and Fe/Eu ions close to +2 and +3, respectively. The material showed direct optical transitions with band gap in the range of 2.25-3.09 eV. The increase of Eu/Ba ratio systematically increased the saturation magnetization from 84.44 emu g-1 to 57.68 emu g-1 at 3 K and 67.09 emu g-1 to 43.42 emu g-1 at 300 K, along with remarkable enhancement of the coercivity (914- 3656 Oe at 3 K and 1996-4862 Oe at 300 K). Electrical conductivity increased from 10-11-10-10 Sm-1 at 30 K to 10-5 -10-4 Sm-1 at 300 K. The electrical conductivity analysis reveals the Efros-Shklovsky-type variable-range hopping mechanism at the low-temperature region, whereas the Mott variable range hopping mechanism is applicable near to room temperature. The analysis of current-voltage characteristics provided electrode to sample interfacial barrier height of 0.27-0.74 eV. The material exhibited novel magneto-electronic properties (bi-stable electronic switching and its transformation in the temperature scale, magnetoresistance and magnetoelectric coupling) which are highly useful for spintronic devices. This work demonstrates that controlled Eu/Ba atomic ratio in the stoichiometric and non-stoichiometric lattice structure could be an effective strategy to widely tune the magnetic, optical and magneto-electronic properties in M-type Ba hexaferrite material.

title: Symmetry-Dependent Polarity Reversal of Bulk Spin-Orbit Torque in Single-Layer MnCoGa
summary: Controlling the magnitude and polarity of spin-orbit torque (SOT) is essential for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices. Here, we realize bulk spin-orbit torque (SOT) in a single-layer Mn1.6Co1.4Ga (MCG) Heusler alloy and achieve lattice strain-controlled reversal of SOT polarity. SOT-driven magnetization switching is achieved over a thickness range of 3-20 nm, with the switching polarity reversed between the strongly strained ultrathin regime and thicker films. First-principles calculations reveal a sizable intrinsic spin Hall conductivity (SHC) in MCG originating from its topological band structure, which is enhanced by the tetragonal distortion without changing sign. Together with the thickness-dependent structural evolution, we demonstrate that the reversal of SOT polarity does not originate from a sign change of the SHC, but rather from lattice distortion induced symmetry breaking that modifies the conversion of spin current into a net bulk SOT, thereby controlling its polarity. These results establish strain-controlled structural symmetry as an additional degree of freedom for tuning bulk SOT in magnetic single layers.

title: Field-Free Reconfigurable Spin Logic in Compositionally Graded MnxCoAl Layer
summary: Spintronic logic-in-memory provides a route to reducing data-transfer energy consumption and accelerating computation by integrating nonvolatile storage and logic functions within a single physical unit. Here, we investigate field-free spin-orbit-torque (SOT) switching and reconfigurable spin logic in a vertically composition-graded MnxCoAl/Pt heterostructure. In contrast to the uniform-composition Mn1.8CoAl/Pt and Mn2.5CoAl/Pt control devices, the Mn1.8-2.5CoAl gradient device exhibits deterministic SOT switching under zero external magnetic field. Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI)-related measurements reveal a finite characteristic effective-field scale, indicating the involvement of chiral magnetization-reversal processes. Meanwhile, the vertical composition gradient introduces magnetic inhomogeneity that can modify domain nucleation and propagation, and the combined effects are consistent with the observed field-free switching behavior. The composition-gradient device further exhibits accumulative multistate switching with stable intermediate Hall-resistance states under zero magnetic field, whereas the uniform-composition controls do not show comparable stable multistate behavior. By tailoring the amplitude, polarity, and sequence of current pulses, the device can be tuned between binary and multilevel switching modes, enabling the experimental realization of AND, OR, NAND, and NOR Boolean operations within the same Hall-bar device without any external magnetic field. These results extend Mn-Co-Al Heusler heterostructures from field-assisted SOT switching toward field-free magnetization control, multistate operation, and reconfigurable spin logic through vertical composition engineering.

title: Enhanced Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect in Nano-Magnetic Metamaterials with Near-Perfect Coherent Absorption
summary: The ability to control magnetic systems without external magnetic fields has attracted attention recently, with all-optical magnetic switching showing increasing promise. Gaining fine control over light-matter interactions in magnetic nanostructures is essential for advancing opto-magnetic technologies, but remains challenging because strong optical coupling must be achieved within ultrathin magnetic structures at the target wavelength. Here, we show that coherent optical interference can increase this interaction in patterned magnetic metasurfaces. Arrays of permalloy nanomagnets are placed on a thin dielectric spacer above a reflective back-plane, forming a magnetic metasurface whose reflected wavefront is defined by the nanomagnet geometry, fill factor, and spacer thickness. Destructive interference between the metasurface and back-plane reflections yields near-perfect absorption, exceeding 95% for circular nanomagnet arrays in both simulation and experiment. The absorbed power is dissipated almost entirely within the nanomagnets, with only a few percent lost in the metallic back-plane. Enhanced absorption is also accompanied by a stronger magneto-optical Kerr effect, driven by both increased light-nanomagnet interaction and reduced reflected background. These results provide a general approach for achieving high optical absorption and strong magneto-optical response in nanoscale magnetic systems, supporting advances in optically addressable spintronics, magnetic sensing, and all-optical magnetic control.

title: Layered spin-crossover metal-organic frameworks for light-induced control of two-dimensional quantum materials
summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann-type spin-crossover (SCO) MOF {FeII(pyS2Et)2[PtII(CN)4]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli-responsive nature of SCO layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few-layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe2) through the strain induced via thermal and light-induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin-valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non-volatile zero-field memory. In NbSe2, light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli-responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain-mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities and extending MOF-based architectures beyond traditional porous-matter applications towards multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

title: Materials and Metrology for Out-of-Plane Damping-Like Spin-Orbit Torque
summary: A new generation of energy-efficient, high-density, and non-volatile memory devices could be enabled if a more efficient mechanism is developed for switching the magnetization orientation of nanoscale magnetic devices possessing perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. A promising strategy under widespread investigation is current-induced damping-like spin-orbit torque with a strong unconventional out-of-plane component, rather than only the conventional in-plane component. In recent years, such torques have been reported in a broad range of materials platforms, arising primarily from three classes of symmetry breaking within the material generating the torque: low crystal symmetry in single-crystalline materials, antiferromagnetic order, and ferromagnetic order. Despite this progress, the field remains fragmented. Measurements using different methods often disagree, artifacts have been misinterpreted, and qualitative observations are sometimes overinterpreted as evidence of technological promise. This Perspective will provide a critical overview of out-of-plane damping-like spin-orbit torques, analyzing the classes of materials which can generate such torques, the experimental methods by which the torques can be quantified, and the progress toward achieving torque efficiencies sufficient for scalable magnetic technologies.

title: Temperature Dependent Evolution of the Electronic Structure in EuZn2As2 across the Neel Transition
summary: Magnetoresistive materials have been tremendously important for the development of magnetic memory storage and spintronic devices. Recently, the antiferromagnetic EuX2Pn2 compounds, with X being a transition metal and Pn being a pnictogen, have seen intensive research interest due to their unusual anomalous Hall effect behavior and pronounced resistive anomaly near the Neel temperature (TN). These magnetotransport phenomena have been interpreted in the context of shortranged ferromagnetic Structuations, magnetic polaron formation, canted spin configurations, and temperature dependent metal insulator transitions in the electronic structure. Here, we report the observation of such a pronounced resistivity anomaly in EuZn2As2 near TN = 19 K. We demonstrate the suppression of this anomaly using applied magnetic fields, both in plane and out of plane. To further interpret the origin of the observed transport behavior, we studied the temperature dependent electronic structure using combined angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and first principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which exhibits limited modifications to the bands across TN away from the Fermi energy. This lack of involvement of the electronic structure indicates a spin-scattering origin of the aforementioned transport properties, rather than a reconstruction of the Fermi surface.

title: Nanodiamond Sensing of Stray Fields during Domain Reversal
summary: Quantitative measurement of nanoscale stray magnetic fields during domain reversal is important for understanding and optimizing magnetic memory and logic devices. Yet, achieving high spatial resolution with minimally invasive probes remains challenging. Here we demonstrate nanodiamonds (NDs) hosting an ensemble nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers as local quantum sensors of domain-reversal stray fields in a CoFeB strip. During magnetic-field-driven reversal, the ND sensors resolve three distinct local responses depending on their positions relative to the strip: a positive frequency jump at the edge, an unexpected negative jump just outside the strip, and a negligible change near the center. These contrasting signals are quantitatively explained by magnetostatic boundary fields from micromagnetic simulations. We further implement a fully constrained fitting procedure for optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, enabling robust field extraction even when resonances are partially resolved. Together, these results establish NV-ND magnetometry as a simple, transferable, and quantitative approach for characterizing spatially heterogeneous magnetic fields in thin-films and spintronic devices.

title: Spin-Polarized Magnetic Metal Electrodes for Magnetic Tunnel Junctions
summary: Magnetic tunnel junctions are foundational components of spintronic memory, sensing, and computing, and their performance depends critically on the magnetic metallic electrodes. This Perspective examines electrode materials through the lens of magnetic order and the distinct microscopic mechanisms that generate spin-selective tunneling. Conventional ferromagnets, including CoFeB and half-metallic Heusler alloys, support exchange-split electronic states and symmetry-filtered tunneling, whereas compensated collinear and noncollinear antiferromagnets exploit sublattice selectivity, spin-orbit anisotropy, vector spin textures, and magnetic multipoles. Altermagnets provide a collinear, zero-net-moment route based on symmetry-allowed momentum-dependent spin splitting. Across these material classes, we compare the origins of tunneling polarization, the roles of barrier evanescent states and interface termination, and strategies for electrically writing and reading the relevant magnetic order. This comparison reveals a broader design principle: effective electrode polarization is not a scalar bulk quantity, but a momentum-, orbital-, symmetry-, and interface-resolved transport property. Beyond the pursuit of ever larger tunneling magnetoresistance, future progress will depend on converting the unconventional spin polarization of emerging magnetic metals into electrically addressable, thermally robust, and reproducible tunneling functionality at realistic interfaces.
